knowledge:
- key_parameters: platform=Character string of the Bioconductor annotation package (e.g., "hgu133a.db") ;; annotate=Character string specifying the category source (e.g., "REACTOME", "GO.ALL", "PFAM") ;; local=Local statistic to assess feature-by-feature association (e.g., "t.Student", "t.Welch", "f.ANOVA", "t.LM", "t.paired") ;; global=Global statistic to measure category-level association (e.g., "Wilcoxon", "AveDiff", "Fisher", "Pearson", "Kolmogorov") ;; method=Resampling method to use (e.g., "permutation", "bootstrap.t", "bootstrap.q", "express") ;; Pi.mat=Number of resamples (default 1000) or a pre-computed resampling matrix; set to 1 to bypass resampling ;; error=Multiple testing correction method (e.g., "FDR.BH", "FDR.YB", "FWER.Bonf", "FWER.Holm", "FWER.WY") ;; Z.mat=An optional matrix of covariates for adjustment ;; parallel=Logical indicating whether to run resampling in parallel
- alternatives: safeExpress=An external package (called via method = "express") that provides analytical approximations of permutation-based tests to greatly reduce computational requirements ;; globaltest=An alternative pathway-analysis tool for survival data, though safe's getCOXresiduals provides a computationally efficient resampling-based alternative ;; GSEA=Uses Kolmogorov-Smirnov-type tests of enrichment; safe can run this via global = "Kolmogorov" but it is computationally intensive
- when_to_use: Use when performing pathway or gene-set enrichment analysis on gene expression data where you want to account for gene-gene correlation using robust resampling-based methods (permutation or bootstrapping) across diverse experimental designs.
- pitfalls: Missing values are not allowed in the expression matrix and must be imputed prior to analysis ;; When passing a character vector as the response, the first unique element becomes Group 1, which defines the direction of differential expression ;; Permutation-based error controls (FDR.YB, FWER.WY) are superior but highly memory and computationally intensive ;; User-defined local statistics can be very slow if they rely on apply loops instead of matrix operations ;; The Kolmogorov-Smirnov global statistic (global = "Kolmogorov") is computationally intensive and may not be feasible for general use

workflows.name: standard_safe_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform resampling-based pathway analysis on two-sample gene expression data using built-in annotations.
workflows.stages: 1. Run safe with platform annotation ;; 2. Tabulate top results using safe.toptable ;; 3. Extract gene-specific results using gene.results ;; 4. Plot pathway results using safeplot
workflows.code:
results <- safe(e3.upp, p3.upp$p53, platform = "hgu133a.db",
                annotate = "REACTOME", print.it = FALSE)
safe.toptable(results, number = 10)
gene.results(results, cat.name = "REACTOME:R-HSA-69183", gene.names = genes)
safeplot(results, cat.name = "REACTOME:R-HSA-69183", gene.names = genes)

workflows.name: custom_cmatrix_safe_analysis
workflows.intent: Build a custom category matrix and run SAFE analysis.
input: genes (named character vector of gene symbols)
workflows.stages: 1. Map gene identifiers to Entrez IDs ;; 2. Build category matrix using getCmatrix ;; 3. Run safe using the custom category matrix
workflows.code:
entrez <- unlist(mget(names(genes),hgu133aENTREZID))
C.mat <- getCmatrix(gene.list = as.list(reactomeEXTID2PATHID),
                    present.genes = entrez,prefix = "REACTOME:",
                    min.size = 10, max.size = 500)
results <- safe(e3.upp, p3.upp$p53, C.mat, print.it = FALSE)

workflows.name: survival_safe_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform pathway analysis for right-censored survival data using martingale residuals.
workflows.stages: 1. Compute Cox residuals using getCOXresiduals ;; 2. Run safe on the residuals
workflows.code:
drop <- is.na(p3.upp$t.rfs)
Xy <- getCOXresiduals(e3.upp[,!drop], p3.upp$t.rfs[!drop], 
                      p3.upp$e.rfs[!drop])
results2 <- safe(Xy$X.star, Xy$y.star, C.mat, 
                 Pi.mat = 1, print.it = FALSE)

workflows.name: covariate_adjusted_safe_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform pathway analysis adjusting for confounding covariates.
workflows.stages: 1. Compute residuals adjusting for covariates using getXYresiduals ;; 2. Run safe on the residuals
workflows.code:
Xy <- getXYresiduals(e3.upp, p3.upp$p53, Z.mat = p3.upp$er)
results2 <- safe(Xy$X.star, Xy$y.star, C.mat, 
                 Pi.mat = 1, print.it = FALSE)
